correctness.rationale: For every finite tree cone the edge-orientation-contraction count is reconstructed exactly from chromatic polynomials, giving coefficient 2·3^(n-2) on tree edges and 2^d·3^(n-1-d) on a spoke at a degree-d tree vertex. The integrated section-edge identity gives the directional quotient with the correct intrinsic support normalization. For path cones the quotient reduces to C(1-J/(3D)); both path triangle inequalities imply 2J≤(n-2)(D-J). Equality analysis proves all claimed optimal normals, and continuity provides the entire interval. No step extrapolates finite tests to all dimensions. Standalone exact checker passed fan orientation/edge counts through n=7, 19496 integer direction equality comparisons, and eight non-path coefficient profiles.

value.rationale: The 2023 motivating literature asks about average vertex counts across parallel sections. Fan graphical zonotopes form an infinite natural family in growing dimension with 2·3^(n-1) vertices and nonconstant slicing complexity. The exact maximum/minimum, limiting anisotropy factor 3/2, and every attaining normal resolve a complete geometric optimization problem rather than a table lookup or arbitrary parameter slice. The broader exact tree-cone formula supplies a structural degree interpretation that may support other natural trees without claiming those unproved optimizations.
